interest: This document provides an intriguing glimpse into how personal interests and diplomatic privileges intersected in U.S.-Japan relations during the interwar era. Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes, an avid equestrian and polo enthusiast, received rare permission directly from the Emperor to tour the Imperial Stud in Hokkaido. Additionally, it highlights State Department filing methodology, demonstrating how substantive reports on specialized subjects like animal husbandry and equine breeding were cross-referenced into subject decimal file 894.62211 from personal diplomatic personnel files.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State Document File Note (cross-reference sheet) filed under decimal number 894.62211, concerning animal husbandry, beasts of burden, and horses in Japan. Dated October 31, 1930, the document references a communication filed under 123 Forbes, W. Cameron/52 from American Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes regarding the horse and horse-breeding situation in Japan. It notes that due to the Ambassador's interest in the subject, the Emperor of Japan granted him permission to visit the Imperial Stud in Hokkaido.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a despatch on the horse and horse-breeding situation in Japan and Ambassador Forbes's visit to the Imperial Stud at Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State Document File Note (cross-reference sheet) dated October 31, 1930, directing researchers to document 123 Forbes, W. Cameron/52. It summarizes a report from Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes concerning horses and the horse-breeding situation in Japan. The note highlights that, because of the Ambassador's personal interest in horses, the Emperor permitted him to visit the Imperial Stud located in Hokkaido.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Horses and Horse-Breeding Situation in Japan
